title: Strided memory-view optimizer introduces token-index skew and softmax bias in multi-stream prefill/decode
creator: Anika Shah
description: Summary: After landing an optimization that rewrites attention kernel tiling as a strided memory-view transformation to improve L2 locality, we are seeing a correctness regression on multi-stream prefill/decode workloads. Symptoms: subtle token-index skew between prefill and decode phases resulting in softmax probability bias, sample drift, and in some cases out-of-bounds KV-store writes under high concurrency. The bug is deterministic on affected hardware+model shapes and appears when the optimizer reorders internal tile iteration order for odd tile strides. This ticket tracks root cause, immediate mitigation, and a fix plus tests and rollout plan.
investigation_summary: Root cause hypothesis: the 'strided memory-view optimizer' creates a new logical view mapping from (batch, head, seq, tile) -> linear buffer index. The mapping omitted the canonical token-offset normalization step that guarantees stable ordering between prefill and decode codepaths. With multi-stream interleaving the optimizer's tile reorder interacts with the decode path's incremental KV append, producing an index skew (off-by-tile) for affected tensors. Numeric consequences: softmax inputs get shuffled late in the pipeline leading to stable but incorrect attention weights (observed as small but systematic probability shifts). Concurrently, certain index calculations (tile_base + stride * slot) overflow bounds in rare shapes, causing occasional OOB writes to KV slab when background allocator aggressively reclaims and repurposes adjacent pages.
repro_steps: Build runtime with CUDA 12.2 and enable STRIDED_MEM_VIEW opt flag
Run model: gpt-medium-like, num_heads=32, head_dim=64, batch=8, seq_prefill=256, decode_steps=128 with multi-stream parallelism=4
Observe: deterministic token-level divergence from baseline after ~18 decode tokens; check token alignment map and attention matrices
Enable runtime debug: export REDWOOD_DEBUG_TILE_MAP=1 to capture mapping dumps for prefill and decode; compare index maps to see off-by-tile shift
logs_and_artifacts: Bisect result: commit 4f2a9b6 introduced strided optimizer (bisection log in gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/eng-59123-bisect)
mitigation: Rollback: Already reverted the optimizer flag in runtime-1.24 candidate for hosted; revert PR #4821 applied to staging
Short-term: gate the strided optimization behind model-shape whitelist (only allow even tile-stride sizes), disable for multi-stream>1
Monitoring: Added alert for token-alignment-delta > 0 at production-smoke-test layer and an OOB write rate SLI
Customer-facing: Notified affected customers via support ticket with recommended pinned runtime version
proposed_fix: Canonical mapping: Add explicit canonical_token_offset normalization to the memory-view transformation to guarantee identical linearization between prefill and decode codepaths
Index sanitization: Add bounds checks and a fast-path sanitizer that validates tile_base computations in debug builds (can be disabled in prod for perf)
Atomic index updates: Protect the KV index table updates with lightweight per-shard CAS to avoid interleaving races when multi-stream writes use reclaimed slabs
Regression tests: Add deterministic multi-stream integration test that compares attention matrices (prefill vs decode) across tiled and non-tiled kernels
Performance validation: Run full perf-suite (latency and throughput) to ensure fixes recover expected gains within 5% of original optimizer target
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests reproduce the original regression and show it is fixed
No OOB KV writes under stress test for 48h on qualification hardware matrix
Perf delta for tiled path is within 5% of pre-regression numbers on benchmark suite
Code review approvals from serving-runtime owners and numeric-stability SME
Rollout plan validated on staging and Dedicated clusters with canary traffic
rollout_plan: Merge fix into runtime-1.24 branch behind 'strided' feature flag
Deploy to staging clusters with 5% traffic for 24h and run smoke and regression suites
Canary to Dedicated (reserved) pools next with increased observability for token-alignment metric
Gradual ramp to 100% over 3 days if no regressions; otherwise rollback to reverted build
Post-rollout: run daily regression check for 7 days and then close the ticket
